THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE K.NATARAJAN  ORAL ORDER Learned High Court Government Pleader is directed to accept notice for the respondent.
This petition is filed by the petitioner-accused No.3 under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. (482 BNSS) for granting anticipatory bail in Crime No.248/2021 of Yelahanka Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 419, 420, 465, 468, 471 read with Section 34 of IPC.
2.
Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.

3. The case of the prosecution is that the complainant - M. Jamuna has filed first information to the police on 24.09.2021 alleging that the site No.454 measuring 30 x 40 sq. ft. has been allotted to her mother-in-law - Bhagirathamma in the year 1972 by the Karnataka State Government.
The State Government also issued Hakkupathra in her name and she NC: 2025:KHC:990 constructed a small house and was enjoying the said property.

The said Bhagirathamma died on 09.04.2017 and after the demise of her mother-in-law, the complainant found the site documents and after verifying the documents in the Sub- Registrar office and Revenue Office, she found that the site No.454 has been divided into two portions by impersonation of her mother-in-law and another woman has got created the documents and executed the sale deeds in favour of accused No.2.
It is further alleged that the accused persons impersonated her mother-in-law and created the documents.
After registering the FIR, the police tried to arrest the accused Nos.4 and 7.

The accused Nos.4 and 7 approached this Court for anticipatory bail and they have been granted anticipatory bail by this Court in Crl.P.No.8788/2021 on 16.12.2021.
4.
The present petitioner is said to be shown as accused No.3 in the charge-sheet and he is apprehending arrest in the hands of police.
Hence, he approached the Sessions Court for grant of anticipatory bail, which came to be rejected.
Hence, he is before this Court.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that accused No.2 was the purchaser of the property from the erstwhile owner and this petitioner is subsequent purchaser from accused No.2 under the registered sale deed.
He is the bonafide purchaser and he is not aware of the previous transaction.
Nothing was seized from this petitioner and he is not required for any interrogation.
The investigation is completed, charge-sheet is filed.
The co-accused persons were already granted anticipatory bail by this Court.
Hence, this petitioner is also entitled for anticipatory bail on the ground of parity.
6. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader objected the petition.

7. Having heard the arguments and on perusal of the records, it is alleged that the accused persons created document and executed the sale deed in favour of accused No.2 by impersonating the mother-in-law of the complainant.
The present petitioner is said to be the subsequent purchaser from accused No.2.
Investigation is completed and charge- sheet is filed.
The co-accused persons have been granted NC: 2025:KHC:990 anticipatory bail by this Court.
Nothing is recovered from this petitioner and he is not required for any interrogation.
Such being the case, the petitioner is entitled for anticipatory bail.
Hence, the following ORDER The petition is allowed.
